notes: Rewrites cancelReusableCaller with hand-rolled caller aggregation that overwrites already-finished nested callers (for example Success) with Cancelled, and always reports the top caller; the emit test is oddly placed in clear_tasks_test.go.

Hand-rolls caller aggregation instead of reusing RefreshReusableCallerStatus, overwrites already-finished nested callers with Cancelled, and always rewrites the top caller; the service test sits in an unrelated test file.

Minimal and mostly right, but it relies on IsExpanded instead of actual children and always reports the caller even when its status did not change; the single-level test passes every job, which likely masks the bug, and the emit path has no test.

Fixes the root cause by re-aggregating expanded callers from their children in cancelOneJob and emits after the settle-only path, but it keys on IsExpanded rather than on actually having children, always reports the caller even when unchanged, and its test cancels every job, which may mask the original bug.

Callers with children now take their status from their children and are reported when it changes, which matches the reference; the refreshRunStatus fallback also unsticks legacy rows on ack, though emitting whenever the run is done can emit twice.

Cleanly re-aggregates callers with children in cancelOneJob, refreshes the run when an unchanged caller absorbs a child update (healing stuck runs), and emits when the run is done; one redundant emit, with good model and service tests.
Works through a cancelCaller closure, but its child-status condition is convoluted, the force-only settle tweak is extra, and the concurrency emit has no test.

Works for the reported case, but cancelCaller's child-status condition is convoluted (it falls back to a direct Cancelled write when all children finished non-cancelled), emit fires whenever the run is done, and there is no service-level test for the concurrency wake-up.

Core fix matches C1, but RefreshReusableCallerStatus now writes the caller and cascades on every child update; it also always settles and emits, and rewrites error messages unrelated to the task to be less informative.

The cancelOneJob re-aggregation fix is right, but RefreshReusableCallerStatus now always writes status on every child update (extra writes, and no cascade on MySQL anyway when affected rows are 0), settle and emit now run unconditionally, and error messages were reworded without need; test coverage is strong, including an integration test.

It stops writing Cancelled early, but returns nil for callers that move to Cancelling, so their transition is never reported (a hidden test fails); it also re-queries all attempt jobs for every caller.

Leaves the caller untouched and returns nil while descendants are cancelling, so the caller's transition is never reported, and it re-queries all attempt jobs per caller; it fails one hidden test even though the emit part matches the reference.

Correct fix with a precise emit condition and thorough tests including legacy stuck states, but changing UpdateRunJob to always refresh the run adds redundant refreshes at every nesting level in a hot path.

Callers with children are derived from them in cancelOneJob, the emit condition is close to the reference, and UpdateRunJob now always refreshes the run so already-stuck rows heal on ack; tests are thorough across the ack, stuck-repair, force and concurrency-wake cases.

Callers stay cancelling but their Cancelling transition is deliberately not reported (a hidden test fails), and EmitJobsIfReadyByJobs is replaced by an unconditional per-run emit while settle now always runs.

settleCaller drops callers that move to Cancelling from the returned job list, so they get no commit status or notification, and it replaces EmitJobsIfReadyByJobs with an unconditional run emit; it fails one hidden test despite decent tests of its own.

It rewrites caller cancellation with hand-rolled status logic that bypasses aggregation and can overwrite an already finished nested caller as Cancelled; the tests are decent, but the service test is placed in clear_tasks_test.go.

Works, but rewrites cancelReusableCaller with a hand-rolled in-memory status aggregation that duplicates RefreshReusableCallerStatus and always rewrites the top caller's stopped time, leaving two sources of truth.

A minimal and clean fix that re-aggregates expanded callers and emits only after a settle-only cancel, but it keys on IsExpanded rather than actual children and always reports the caller; its single-level test passes all jobs, which can mask the bug on sqlite, and there is no emit test.

A small, targeted fix: expanded callers are re-aggregated from their children instead of being written Cancelled, and the run is emitted after a settle; however, an unchanged caller is still reported as updated, and the test passes every job, which on SQLite can hide the bug.

Callers with children are re-aggregated instead of being written Cancelled, and a no-op caller refresh still refreshes the run (which also repairs already-stuck rows); the emit condition is broader than needed and can emit twice.

Clean and minimal: callers with children are re-aggregated and reported only when changed, an unchanged caller still refreshes the run, and a done run is emitted (slightly redundantly); good model and service tests.

It works, but the caller-handling closure has an odd child-status condition, it changes force-cancel to always settle with a misleading comment, and it can emit twice; it adds only a model test and no concurrency emit test.

The fix works through a caller-refresh closure and a run refresh when the caller is unchanged, but the child-status heuristic for when to cancel a caller directly is odd, and there is no test for the concurrency emit.

The main caller fix is sound, but RefreshReusableCallerStatus now always rewrites the caller (extra writes, and fragile where MySQL reports 0 affected rows), plus it always settles, always emits and churns error messages; it does add an integration test.

The cancelOneJob caller fix is correct, but forcing a no-op status write in RefreshReusableCallerStatus is a DB-dependent hack that may not cascade on MySQL, and the patch also renames unrelated error messages and emits on every cancel; tests are extensive, including an integration test.

It leaves callers untouched while a descendant is cancelling, so the run settles, but it drops their Running->Cancelling transition from the returned updates (no notifications or commit statuses for callers) and fails one hidden test.
Skips writing a caller that has a cancelling descendant but returns nil, so the caller's transition is never reported; it also loads all attempt jobs per caller and fails a hidden test.

Callers with children follow their aggregate, and the emit condition closely matches the reference; however, UpdateRunJob now refreshes the run after every parent cascade, a broader change that causes redundant refreshes in nested chains, though the tests are thorough.

Callers with children are refreshed instead of cancelled, UpdateRunJob now always refreshes the run (redundant but robust), and the emit condition closely matches the reference; strong tests cover acknowledgement, stale-state repair and concurrency wake-up.
It settles callers from their children but does not report callers that become Cancelling, and it replaces EmitJobsIfReadyByJobs with an unconditional run emit; it fails one hidden test.
Database state is right, but callers moving to Cancelling are not reported in the returned jobs, EmitJobsIfReadyByJobs is replaced by an unconditional per-run emit, and it fails a hidden test.
